per_shot.subjects: per-subject representation (character_id plus the fields above)

per_shot: source_media per element (captured vs generated, recorded honestly)
representation.rule:
Two subjects in one shot may carry different representations (e.g. a
photorealistic digital human talking with a stylized 3D creature);
two shots in one production may carry different representations (e.g.
a flat-2D explainer scene followed by a live-action plate). A single
subject in a single shot carries exactly one value per dimension.

compatible_layers.description:
Layers that do not conflict combine freely: voice-consistency,
humanized-production, language-authenticity, production-systems,
emotional-performance, and resource-management combine with any
primary pathway. A production routinely runs many layers at once.

precedence_tie_breaking.description:
Where two layers both speak to the same decision, the routing
matrix's precedence order decides which one speaks first; the
other still applies where it does not contradict. Command
authority remains the router (precedence 1): it routes, it does
not generate.

primary_pathway.description:
One primary pathway per production, chosen from the production's
dominant medium and purpose (e.g. kids-family-animation /
cinematic-power for a stylized 3D short; realistic-person for a
photorealistic digital-human video; live-action-vfx for a
live-action-plus-creature video). The primary pathway supplies the
production's main rules; it does not own the production exclusively.

style_profiles.description:
One or more visual-style profiles layer onto the primary pathway
(e.g. the flat-2D explainer profile, an anime profile). A profile
contributes its style lock, palette, and craft rules; it never
vetoes an unrelated layer. A profile's style lock binds the shots
it covers, per subject per shot — see true_conflicts TC-3/TC-4/TC-5.

subject_capabilities.description:
Subject capabilities layer per subject: animal and creature
performance, real-animal handling, age performance, instrument
performance, and similar capabilities apply to the subjects they
describe, in the shots those subjects appear in. Articulation
follows the subject's own anatomy — see true_conflicts TC-1/TC-10.

true_conflicts_only.description:
A conflict exists only when two rules genuinely cannot both hold
for the same subject in the same shot. The absence of a stated
conflict is not a conflict. A conflict is resolved by choosing
per shot (or per subject), recording the choice, and never by
silently dropping a rule. See true_conflicts below.

sequential_chains.name: video-regeneration
sequential_chains.note:
video-regeneration BRACKETS the workflow rather than sitting only at
the end: its §1 complete reference analysis runs FIRST (before any
generation), the foundation skills then supply identity/voice/planning/
humanization, and its §8 mandatory QC runs LAST. Working order,
always: analyse, plan, generate, inspect and correct (video-regeneration
intro; §9).

true_conflicts.resolution: choose per subject per shot — real behaviour OR anthropomorphic direction — and record the choice.
true_conflicts.rule:
Real-animal non-speaking performance cut from real behaviour
(live-action-vfx §6) vs anthropomorphic speaking-animal/creature
direction (cinematic-power §2). A real animal must not be directed
to speak with human lips, and a real animal and a CG creature must
not be mixed into one animal (live-action-vfx §6).

true_conflicts.resolution: choose per subject per shot — captured footage OR generated digital human — and record the choice; record source_media honestly per element.
true_conflicts.rule:
Captured live-action footage of a real shoot (live-action-vfx: real
footage is the input) vs a generated digital human from a still
photo (realistic-person §6: neither animation nor live-action
footage). A generated element is never passed off as captured, and
captured footage is never described as generated (source honesty).

true_conflicts.resolution: choose the style per shot and record it; other cinematic-power layers (music-beat, title cards) may still apply to other shots.
true_conflicts.rule:
Flat-2D-vector style lock (explainer-animation §1, §7) vs anime /
stylized-3D / photorealistic styling (cinematic-power §1 style-lock
choices). One shot cannot hold both style locks.

true_conflicts.resolution: choose the representation per subject per shot and record it.
true_conflicts.rule:
Flat-2D-vector explainer profile vs photorealistic-digital-human
(realistic-person intro). One subject in one shot cannot be both a
flat 2D vector figure and a photorealistic digital human.
true_conflicts.scope: same subject, same shot, visual_style dimension

true_conflicts.resolution: choose the style per shot and record it.
true_conflicts.rule:
Flat-2D explainer profile (explainer-animation §1: no anime
styling, no 3D look, no photorealism; the two character designs
kept apart) vs an anime / 3D / photorealistic kids-family style in
the same shot. A flat-2D kids-family scene does NOT conflict — the
conflict is only the style values in the same shot.

true_conflicts.resolution: choose the representation per subject per shot and record it.
true_conflicts.rule:
Animated character (kids-family-animation §2) vs photorealistic
digital human from a real person's photo (realistic-person §1).
One subject in one shot cannot be both.
true_conflicts.scope: same subject, same shot, visual_style dimension

true_conflicts.resolution: choose the representation per subject per shot and record it.
true_conflicts.rule:
2D/3D-animation styling (cinematic-power §1: 2D anime, 3D stylized
CG) vs photorealistic digital human (realistic-person §6: not
2D/3D animation). One subject in one shot cannot be both.
true_conflicts.scope: same subject, same shot, visual_style dimension

true_conflicts.resolution: choose per subject — synthetic spokesperson OR real-person digital human — and record the choice; consent rules for the real-person path still apply.
true_conflicts.rule:
Synthetic spokesperson who must never resemble a real person
(agency-advertising §5) vs a photorealistic digital human built
from a real person's photo (realistic-person §1). One subject
cannot be both synthetic and a real person's likeness.

true_conflicts.resolution: choose the medium per shot and record it.
true_conflicts.rule:
Flat-2D-vector explainer profile vs captured live-action footage
in the same shot (explainer-animation intro: none of anime, 3D CG,
live-action, music video, or trailer; live-action-vfx: real
footage is the input). One shot cannot be both flat 2D vector and
captured live-action footage.

true_conflicts.resolution: set articulation_target per subject from its anatomy (schemas/character.json, schemas/performance-plan.json); reject a line whose articulation target contradicts its subject.
true_conflicts.rule:
Articulation target must match the subject's own anatomy:
human-mouth-lips only for human/digital-human subjects, bird-beak
for birds, animal-muzzle for animals, creature-jaw-mandibles for
creatures. Human lip-sync on a bird (or beak articulation on a
human) is invalid. This is a dimension rule, not a skill-vs-skill
exclusion — the three skills constrain it jointly, so it is not
mirrored in any single skill's `conflicts` list.
true_conflicts.scope: same subject, same shot (per dialogue line)
